prompt: Plan one concrete Saturday for two friends in the fictional city of Northbridge. Total budget: 3,500 credits. One person has a knee injury: no long standing, steep stairs, or more than 35 minutes of walking total. No calls or advance booking. Weather may turn to heavy rain. Include food and one genuinely unusual activity; transit must stay under 45 minutes each way. They already rejected cinema, the central museum, malls, bowling, and a generic board-game cafe. Treat this catalog as complete and current: A) Central cinema, 2,600, indoor, accessible, tried; B) Central museum, 1,800, indoor, 60-minute standing queue, tried; C) Library risograph demonstration, free, indoor, accessible seating, 14:00–15:15, no booking, 18 minutes from home; D) Covered flea market with seated restoration demonstrations, 500, indoor, mostly accessible, 12:00–17:00, 31 minutes from home; E) Rooftop history walk, free, outdoor, stairs, 20 minutes from home; F) Board-game cafe, 3,200, booking required, tried; G) University robotics open lab, free, indoor, accessible, 16:00–17:00, no booking, 35 minutes from home; H) Riverside food hall, typical meal for two 1,800, indoor, accessible, 8 minutes from C and 12 minutes from G; I) Pottery workshop, 4,000, booking required; J) neighborhood photo scavenger route, free, outdoor, 40 minutes walking. Give the best itinerary, one materially different fallback, why they beat the obvious options, and exact continue/abort checks.
hard_constraints: knee-safe: no steep stairs, long standing, or >35 minutes total walking
must survive uncertain rain through a fallback
include food and an unusual activity
use only the supplied catalog as current fact
must_not_repeat_or_do: invent a venue or current availability

prompt: A payment service occasionally charges the same order twice. Client retries are mandatory. The downstream provider is non-idempotent and sometimes times out after accepting a charge. Logs have no stable request ID. You cannot change the database schema or the provider this week, but Redis already exists and the fix must be deployable and reversible within one day. The team already tried a process-local mutex, longer timeouts, fewer retries, and exponential backoff. Find and rank practical routes around the actual failure windows. The top route must include a minimal falsification test, observable signal, stop/rollback rule, and fallback. Do not answer only with the label ‘make it idempotent.’
hard_constraints: deployable and reversible within one day

prompt: A privacy-focused workflow app has weak week-2 retention. In the last cohort, 42% never completed import, 31% abandoned at a broad permissions screen, and users who created and exported one useful artifact retained 3.2x more often; these are correlations, not proven causes. In one sprint, improve evidence and retention without paid acquisition, discounts, a new core feature, more push notifications, or a full onboarding redesign. The team already tried generic onboarding tips, badges, reminders, and a referral program. Rank practical routes, preserve causal uncertainty, and give the cheapest discriminating test, success/stop signal, and fallback for the winner.
hard_constraints: do not claim correlation proves causation

prompt: Design and rank comeback mechanisms for a competitive strategy game. A losing player may not receive free resources, free units, hidden stat buffs, or lower prices. No new art can be produced. Expert players should exploit the mechanism better than beginners, spectators must understand it, and deliberately falling behind early must not become optimal. The team already rejected rubber-banding resources, a catch-up unit, and hidden dynamic difficulty. Return practical rule/UI changes, the exploit or failure mode of each, a cheap playable test, success/stop criterion, and explain why the top mechanism is not merely disguised rubber-banding.
hard_constraints: no hidden stat buffs or lower prices
must not reward deliberate early losing

prompt: Re-cut one existing 60-second product demo into three clips of at most 20 seconds for skeptical engineers, budget-owning executives, and social viewers. No new footage, voice-over, product claim, metric, or testimonial may be added. Available source beats are: 8s problem scene; 12s uncut workflow; 8s architecture diagram; 7s latency measurement with exact number; 10s before/after operator action; 6s security limitation; 9s logo and generic closing. The team already tried the same cut with different captions, faster pacing, and louder music. Propose a production-ready edit system that makes the three clips structurally distinct while preserving factual nuance. Rank the strongest approach, provide timecoded edit decisions, a review signal, stop condition, and fallback.
hard_constraints: no new claim, metric, testimonial, footage, or voice-over
preserve the security limitation where omission would mislead

prompt: In Toolbox 4.2, the documented command `toolbox inspect --json-output report.json` fails because the release notes in this fixture state that `--json-output PATH` was renamed to `--output PATH --format json`; all other behavior is unchanged. Give exactly one correction, one verification, and one rollback or fallback. Do not offer a portfolio or research plan.
hard_constraints: use only the supplied release-note fact

prompt: Migrate search reads from a monolith to a new service while traffic is continuous. Old and new ranking outputs differ legitimately, rollback must take under one minute, only two engineers are available, and users must not see data inconsistency caused by dual writes. A big-bang cutover, a percentage feature flag without stable cohorts, and dual-writing every mutation were rejected. Find a staged, reversible route with evidence gates, a divergence policy, rollback semantics, and the smallest first slice that teaches something decision-relevant.
hard_constraints: no user-visible inconsistency from dual writes

prompt: Using the evaluation date and timezone in the run manifest, find one genuinely unusual Saturday plan in central Moscow for two adults on the next Saturday. Total all-in budget is 5,000 RUB; no alcohol, no phone calls, no more than 25 minutes walking at a time, and every required reservation or ticket must have a direct online route. They already rejected cinema, mainstream museums, malls, bowling, karaoke, and generic restaurants. Give one best plan and one materially different fallback. Do not declare a slot available unless a current direct source confirms it; otherwise label the gap and give the cheapest verification route. Include checked timestamps, total cost, logistics, cancellation risk, and a go/no-go threshold.
hard_constraints: direct online route for every required ticket
must_not_repeat_or_do: stale aggregator as proof of availability
